Adatum: Joseph Mwangi (Service Desk Manager) asked to add Spanish-language support for their Madrid office, 60 users, from January.

give me a rough scope outline for a data platform cost review, 4 weeks, 1 engineer

what's a reasonable counter? we've had about 4% wage inflation this year

Woodgrove: tabletop exercise booked for 17 Nov, 9am-12pm at their HQ. Ahmed will invite the exec team.
prep me a draft agenda for the 3-hour tabletop for Ahmed
Proseware: Katarzyna approved the testing extension, PO coming this week
Coho: site survey confirmed for 21 Oct, Lucia will meet us on site

Contoso weekly DC exit sync w/ Mark Ellison (IT Director) and Ishani Deshmukh (Infrastructure Mgr, she runs the cutovers day to day). 140 VMs leaving the Naperville data centre in 3 waves. Wave 1 is 32 VMs, non-prod plus the intranet, cutover Sat 21 Feb. Naperville lease ends 30 June and Mark has zero appetite to extend.

Wingtip Toys catch-up w/ Callum Fraser (VP Ecommerce) and Nnamdi Eze (IT Director). Holiday peak recap: 99.95% uptime apart from the 47 min checkout outage on Black Friday, which Callum still brings up on every call. Our managed platform contract ($612k/yr, hosting + 24x7 platform support) renews 30 April.

Proseware renewal is coming up fast. Our CloudOps contract (managed Azure for their policy and claims platforms) ends 31 Mar, current ACV $410k. Duncan Kilbride (Head of Cloud & Infrastructure) is happy with us, but Bianca Moretti in vendor mgmt says anything over $250k goes to competitive review this year.

Wide World Importers rollout steering this morning w/ Stavros Dimitriou (COO, exec sponsor) and Clifford Abara (Head of IT, owns devices + network). Handheld scanner + WMS mobile rollout, 310 devices across 4 DCs: Dallas go-live Mon 16 Feb, then Memphis 9 Mar, Savannah 6 Apr, Reno 27 Apr. Our fee is $860k, billed per DC at each go-live. Stavros wants a go/no-go call the Thursday before each one.

Northwind call w/ Anton Kovalenko (Head of Transport) and Gianna Benedetti (Harrisburg depot manager). Cold-chain pilot: temp + door sensors on 40 refrigerated trucks out of Harrisburg, alerts straight to dispatch. 6 weeks from Mon 9 Feb, $36k fixed fee. Harrisburg pays out about $38k a month in credits for warm deliveries, target is to cut that by 30%.

Woodgrove Bank Jan service desk numbers: 18,400 tickets, FCR 68%, CSAT 4.1. Contract is $1.15M ACV for 2,300 users and renews 30 Jun. Teodora Constantin (Head of IT Ops) told me she wants FCR above 72% before we even start renewal talks.

Fourth Coffee renewal kickoff with Sunita Varghese (procurement mgr). Store Care contract (service desk + store network/POS support for 212 cafes) is $1.38M/yr and renews 17 Apr. We plan to go in at a 6% uplift - they added 40 cafes last year and our field tech wages are up. Sunita wants our proposal by Fri 13 Feb.
also from Sunita: their CFO Philippa Achterberg wants every commercial change shown as a redline against the current contract. No fresh proposal decks, she won't read them.

Adatum: Lourdes Pineda (their service desk manager) sent the January numbers. First call resolution 61% vs 70% target, avg speed to answer 94s vs 60s. Czech queue is the worst by far. Service credit for Jan comes to $14,200. Corinne Haas, our SDM, is pulling root causes.

Proseware observability pilot agreed w/ Duncan. 6 weeks, $18k fixed fee, credited back if they buy the full service. 20 claims platform services in scope, kickoff planned Mon 9 Feb. Raf Quintero (cloud platform mgr) is their lead. Success criteria: alert noise down 50%, MTTR down 30% from the 47 min baseline.

Litware new-year kickoff with Annika Holm (VP Eng) and Deepa Venkatesan (Head of QA). Our QA automation SOW: 12 FTE at $52/hr blended, ~$1.19M/yr, renews 31 March. Annika wants to keep all 12 but move 3 onto performance testing before their April payroll peak. She prefers Slack for day to day, not email.

Trey Research: Dr. Shirin Farrokh (Head of Research IT) rang. January Azure bill came in at $61k vs their $48k monthly budget, a GPU cluster was left running 9 days after a protein-folding batch. Their CFO, Cornelius Ashdown, is asking questions. She needs our explanation by Wed.

Tailspin intro call tmrw 11:00 with Lorraine Pettigrew, their CFO. First time I'm meeting her. Background: we run their contact centre platform plus 24x7 support, $31.8k/month, renews 21 April. Bettina Sorensen (Director of Customer Care) is our champion. What should I ask Lorraine to understand how she's thinking about the renewal?

Lucerne Publishing royalties migration update from Nkechi Obi (Royalties & Contracts Mgr): data mapping about 70% done, cutover still planned for 6 Apr. Spring royalty statements to ~4,800 authors have to go out of the new system by 30 Apr, zero slack on that date.

Woodgrove Win11 migration: Pavel Hrabal (EUC lead) says the Jan pilot on 120 devices went fine, only 3 rollbacks. Main rollout begins Mon 16 Feb with the North region branches (410 devices), then Central from 9 Mar. 1,850 devices in total, fixed price $640k.

Draft a short email to Ishani at Contoso: let's walk through the wave 1 runbook together Thu 5 Feb at 10:00, and can her network team send over the firewall change ticket numbers before the 21 Feb cutover.

Email from Leopold Varga, Litware CFO. He wants 15% off the QA SOW at renewal, their FY26 budgets lock in April. Annika warned me he doesnt take vendor calls at all - email only, and he wants the cost in the subject line so he can triage. noted

draft a note to Shirin on the Azure overrun. The $13k is on us, our runbook had no auto-shutdown on the GPU pool. Fix: auto-stop after 4 hrs idle, budget alerts at 80% and 100%. Say we'll come back with a credit proposal by Thursday. Short, no excuses.

Prep me for Thursday's call with Saskia de Vries, Wingtip's procurement manager. She's new to our contract. I want to walk her through the renewal mechanics: 60-day notice, so anything has to be agreed by 1 March, otherwise it auto-renews on 30 April at the 6% rate card uplift. What will procurement push on?

Tailspin: Lorraine call went well. Big one: she wants all pricing quoted per quarter, never monthly, their budgets run quarterly. So today we're $95.4k a quarter. She'd go 3 years if support for the new Amazon Connect platform is bundled and the Q4 seasonal agents are covered. Shannon Mercer (procurement lead) runs the paperwork.

Fourth Coffee kiosk pilot planning w/ Reggie Mulcahy (VP Retail Ops) and Ezra Pemberton (IT Director). 12 Portland cafes, 2 self-order kiosks each, start Mon 9 Feb, runs 6 weeks. Success = avg ticket +8%, peak queue time -20%, kiosk uptime 99%. Our integration fee is $96k fixed. Ezra wants a PCI scan of the card readers before go-live.
Reggie: never book him 7-10am, that's the morning rush and he's out in stores. He'd rather do a quick Teams call than a long email thread.

Lucerne: Felix Brandauer (Head of Digital) wants a proof of concept for AI metadata tagging on their backlist, 24k titles. $15k is the most he can sign without going to Wilhelmina Strathearn, their CFO. He wants a proposal by Fri 13 Feb.

Draft a quick internal note to Corinne: before I meet Bogdan Ilic (Adatum CIO) tomorrow I need the Jan SLA miss broken down by queue (EN/ES/CZ), the top 3 root causes, and what the $14,200 credit is made of. Need it by 9am.

Northwind: email from Fatma Yilmaz (Vendor Manager). Our managed network contract (SD-WAN + depot Wi-Fi, 4 depots plus HQ, $22.4k/month) renews 18 May. She wants a 3-year proposal by Fri 20 Feb and is opening at 12% off. Also wants the Wi-Fi refreshed at Erie and Scranton.

prep me for Thursday 11am with Ottilie Marchbank, Proseware's CFO. She joined in Sept and I've only met her once. Agenda is the CloudOps renewal ($410k ACV, ends 31 Mar) and vendor mgmt's competitive review. What will she care about and what should I ask her?

WWI wifi survey results from Dallas: dead zones in the cold store, aisles 40-52. Jolanta Nowicka (Dallas DC ops manager) says handhelds drop out every few mins in the freezer section. We need 6 extra access points, change order $14,800 incl. install. Has to be in by 12 Feb or the 16 Feb go-live is at risk.

draft the change order cover email to Clifford: 6 extra APs for the Dallas cold store, $14,800 incl. install, need his approval by Fri so the kit ships in time to install by 12 Feb. Make clear the 16 Feb go-live depends on it.

Draft the agenda for the Woodgrove QBR on Tue 10 Feb, 10-12 at their HQ. Harriet Wanjiru (CIO), Teodora and Pavel attending. Items: Jan service desk stats (FCR 68%, CSAT 4.1), FCR improvement plan, Win11 readiness for the 16 Feb start, renewal timeline to 30 Jun. Keep it tight.

Met Bogdan Ilic. Calm but very clear. He wants a written service improvement plan by Fri 13 Feb, with measures he can track weekly. Every meeting needs an agenda in the calendar invite at least 24h before or he declines it, that's his rule for all vendors. Service desk contract ($1.85M/yr, 2,300 users across Columbus, Monterrey and Brno) ends 30 June. They decide by 31 March: 3-yr extension or go to tender.

Contoso: first proper meeting with Evangeline Rourke, their CFO. She owns the DC exit business case. If they're not out of Naperville by 30 June the lease rolls month to month at $62k. Her rule for anything we send her: open with the cost of doing nothing, then our ask. Otherwise she stops reading.

fyi Raf Quintero at Proseware wants everything operational in the shared slack channel #proseware-ops, he ignores email in his on-call weeks. Also their CISO Yusuf Demir has to approve the monitoring agent install before the pilot can start. Raf says he's thorough but slow.

Tailspin: Bettina and Kelsey Monroe (IT Director) walked me through the Avaya to Amazon Connect move. 160 agents. Pilot with the warranty claims team (40 agents) from Mon 23 Feb, the other 120 in waves after that. Jan abandonment was 9.2% vs their 5% target. Kelsey wants a written status at 4pm Mountain every day of a cutover week, nothing in between unless it's a P1.

Lucerne: Nkechi prefers calls after 2pm, mornings she's buried in author and agent queries. Also realised she's the only person there who really understands the old royalty rules (escalators, reserves against returns). Single point of failure for the migration.
Trey: agreed w/ my VP we'll credit half the overrun, $6,500, on the Feb invoice. Shirin is fine with that. Auto-stop and budget alerts went live today.

Wingtip: Beatrix Thornquist (CFO) joined the end of my call with Callum. FY26 IT services budget is down 8% and she wants the renewal flat, no uplift. Important: any pricing for her goes as a simple table in the email body. No attachments, no decks, she reads everything on her phone between meetings.

Draft a 45-min kickoff agenda for the Northwind cold-chain pilot, Fri 6 Feb at Harrisburg. Anton, Gianna, 2 of her dispatchers, our IoT lead. Scope (40 trucks), what an alert looks like and who acts on it, how we baseline the $38k/month in credits, weekly readouts, what happens at week 6.

Saskia call done. Wingtip policy is 3 quotes for any contract over $500k, so she's getting 2 benchmark quotes for hosting + support. 'Not an RFP', she says. She wants our current SLA schedule and the 2025 incident log by 13 Feb.

Kiosk readiness call w/ Ezra at 2pm. Prep me: what to check on PCI scope for the card readers, firmware versions, what happens to orders if a kiosk loses network, and the rollback plan if a cafe has problems on day one.

Northwind: sensor supplier just told us the shipment slipped, now lands Wed 11 Feb. Install is about 4 days across 40 trucks, so the Mon 9 Feb start is gone. Realistic start is the week after. Kickoff tomorrow still goes ahead, Gianna is fine with it.

Litware: Annika asked if we can help with SOC 2 Type II evidence collection, their compliance manager left in Jan and the audit window opens 1 April. Rough ask is 1 analyst for 8 weeks. I ballparked $36k. She needs a decision by 20 Feb, Gareth Pryce (their vendor manager) will paper it.

Just off with Ottilie Marchbank. She wants a 2-yr option priced, wants to see pilot results before signing anything, and anything commercial has to be in her inbox the evening before - she reads email at 7am ahead of her 8:30 exec meeting. I floated a 5% uplift, she didnt love it.

Contoso runbook review with Ishani done. Wave 2 = 58 VMs (claims apps) on Sat 11 Apr, wave 3 = 50 VMs (policy admin + data warehouse) on Sat 16 May. Leaves about 6 weeks of buffer before the lease ends. Our Naperville infra support contract ends 15 June, the other date to watch.

Help me outline the Adatum service improvement plan (SIP) Bogdan wants by the 13th. Issues: FCR 61%, ASA 94s, Czech queue understaffed, knowledge articles way out of date (Corinne found 40% untouched since 2023). Practical, weekly measures he can track. Not a consultancy deck.

Woodgrove: Josh Tremblay (third-party risk mgr) emailed. Their regulator wants a documented exit plan for every critical outsourced service, ours (service desk) is due 31 Mar. Plus a 120-question due diligence questionnaire, due 27 Feb.

Fourth Coffee readiness: only 14 of 24 kiosks have arrived, the rest are due Tue. So pilot start slips from Mon 9 Feb to Wed 11 Feb. PCI scan booked for Mon 9 Feb. Ezra wants offline mode tested at 2 cafes before launch.

Trey: Shirin warned me Cornelius Ashdown never approves anything over $100k by email. He wants a 20-min call with the numbers on screen, Thursdays after 3pm only. The phase 2 SOW goes to him next week.
Tailspin: Bettina wants the monthly KPI pack to show abandonment by queue (warranty, orders, tech support) from the Feb pack on. Passed it to our WFM analyst, easy add.
Draft my reply to Leopold on the 15% ask. Dont concede anything yet, just say we'll come back with options by Fri 13 Feb, one of which reduces team size. Remember his rules on format.

Trey contract facts so I stop digging: Research Cloud Ops (managed Azure + support) is $520k/yr and renews 15 May. Lab Data Platform phase 2 SOW is $410k - 14 instrument connectors, ELN integration, GxP validation pack. Kickoff targeted Mon 16 Feb.

Draft the proposal summary for Felix's metadata POC: 2,000 backlist titles as the sample, 4 weeks, we generate BISAC subject codes + keywords, accuracy target 85% against his editors' own tags. $14.5k fixed so he can sign it himself under his $15k limit.

Wingtip: Tobias Kranz (Head of Demand Planning) wants a forecasting pilot. Their 8-week forecast error is ~34% MAPE and they overstocked plush by $1.1M last Christmas. Idea: 6 weeks, 3 product lines (plush, puzzles, outdoor). Hugo Lam from our data science team is scoping it.

draft a quick note to Reggie confirming the new kiosk pilot start, Wed 11 Feb, all 12 cafes. Remaining 10 kiosks land Tue and get installed overnight, PCI scan Mon. Offer a 10-min Teams call Tue afternoon if he wants a walkthrough.

Contoso: Niamh Cassidy (CISO) pinged me. Nothing production moves to Azure until there's an independent pen-test of the landing zone. Not in our SOW and Mark didn't know about it. Wave 1 is mostly non-prod but the intranet counts as prod, so this hits 21 Feb.

WWI: Clifford approved the AP change order on the phone, PO to follow. Maeve Abernathy (procurement) confirmed the EDI migration RFP is out: responses due Fri 20 Feb noon, decision targeted 6 Mar. They're moving 62 trading partners off their old VAN.

draft the pilot kickoff post for #proseware-ops (Raf + team) for Mon 9 Feb: 20 claims services in scope, 6 weeks, targets alert noise -50% and MTTR -30% vs the 47 min baseline. Mention we still need Yusuf's sign-off on the agent install. Short, it's slack.

Jakub Hora (IT lead at Adatum's Brno plant) emailed, pretty angry. Czech callers are waiting 6+ min at the 6am shift change. He wants a Czech speaker on L1 from 5:30. Corinne says we can add 2 Czech-speaking agents but earliest start is 2 March.

Northwind kickoff at Harrisburg done, good energy, the dispatchers get it. Anton doesn't want email updates: he wants 10 mins at his Monday 11:30 transport huddle, every week. Gianna runs the pilot readout with us Thursdays at 2pm.

Litware Playwright migration: rollout started on 9 Feb (today), payroll module first. Bartek Zielinski, our lead automation engineer, is running it. 1,400 Selenium tests to migrate by end of April. Benefits module is next, planned for 2 March.

Prep me for Thursday's 3:30 call with Cornelius Ashdown on the phase 2 SOW ($410k). He'll bring up the Azure overrun too. Give me the numbers in the order he'll want them, likely objections, and what I can concede.

Lucerne: Linus Penhaligon (IT Mgr) told me Wilhelmina Strathearn sent back our last SOW unread because it was a PDF. She wants Word docs so she can track-change them. So every commercial doc for her goes in Word from now on.

Marguerite Castellano (WWI CFO) pushed back on the $14,800 AP change order. Her view: our original survey missed the cold store so we should eat half. Also fyi she wants every cost split by DC in an Excel attachment, never typed into the email body.

Scoping call with Tobias at 2pm on the Wingtip pilot. What do I need to nail down? Thinking success metric (target MAPE), access to POS + web store order data, an owner on their side, and price. Hugo reckons $48k fixed for the 6 weeks.

Draft a note to Mark at Contoso flagging Niamh's pen-test requirement. Not in our SOW, and since the intranet in wave 1 counts as prod it could hit the 21 Feb cutover. Propose a CR to bring in a pen-test firm, roughly $18-20k. Friendly, not defensive.

Proseware pilot did NOT start today. Yusuf Demir hasn't approved the agent install, he wants our latest pen test summary first. Sent it at 11. Raf thinks Wed is realistic, so the pilot end date moves too.
PCI scan on the kiosk card readers came back with 2 low findings (default SNMP string, an old TLS cipher on 3 units). Ezra's team is fixing tonight. Still go for Wed.

Renewal kickoff with Shannon Mercer at Tailspin tmrw 2pm. We're at $95.4k/qtr, renews 21 April, Lorraine is open to 3 yrs if Connect support and the Q4 seasonal agents are in. What's my opening position and what should I hold back?

prep me for tmrw's Woodgrove QBR. Harriet will push on FCR (68% vs the 72% Teodora wants). I also want to plant the MDR idea - Teodora let slip their SOC provider contract ends 31 Aug and Harriet is unhappy with their response times. Who cares about what in that room?
Adatum: when exactly does Bogdan want the improvment plan, and what was his rule about how meetings with him get set up?
ugh, WWI: the AP vendor says the 6 access points won't arrive until 17 Feb. Dallas go-live slips from 16 Feb to Mon 23 Feb. Stavros grumbled but agreed, as long as Memphis stays 9 Mar.

draft a short update to Stavros and Jolanta: Dallas go-live now Mon 23 Feb because the APs land 17 Feb, install 17-18 Feb, coverage test Thu 19 Feb morning ahead of the go/no-go. Memphis still 9 Mar. Ask Jolanta to keep the training slots in the week of 16 Feb as dry runs.

Tobias agreed: $48k fixed, 6 weeks, target MAPE under 25% on the 8-week horizon for the 3 lines. Data extract from POS + web store by Friday. Start Mon 16 Feb if the SOW is signed this week. Anything over $40k needs Beatrix's signature.
Contoso: Ishani's network team sent teh firewall tickets, 14 rule changes, all approved for the 21 Feb window. One less blocker, assuming the pen-test thing gets sorted.

Woodgrove QBR done. Harriet happy with CSAT, not with FCR. We agreed to add 2 L2 engineers for 8 weeks at our cost to push knowledge articles. Harriet wants an MDR proposal by 13 Mar, budget around $300k/yr. Teodora: for any P1 she wants a phone call first, email after, never email only.

draft the QBR follow-up email to Harriet Wanjiru, cc Teodora: thanks for teh time, 2 extra L2 engineers for 8 weeks at our cost on knowledge articles, FCR target 72% by end of March, MDR proposal by 13 Mar, exit plan to Josh by 31 Mar.

Draft the options email to Leopold Varga for Friday. Option A: keep 12 FTE at $50/hr on a 2-year term. Option B: 10 FTE at $51/hr, also 2-year. Show annual cost and saving vs the current $1.19M for each. Cost in the subject line like he wants.
Tailspin: Shannon wants 10% off for a 3-yr commitment, and the Q4 seasonal seats (60 extra agents, Oct-Dec) priced as a seperate option. Needs our proposal by Fri 27 Feb. I didn't commit to anything.

Lucerne steerco: Linus says the AS/400 extract has 11,000 contract records with the territory fields missing. Nkechi reckons 3 weeks of manual cleanup and she's the only one who can do it. 6 Apr cutover now at risk.
Beatrix signed the forecasting pilot SOW last night, $48k. Start Mon 16 Feb confirmed. Tobias owns it on their side, Hugo on ours. Midpoint readout pencilled for Fri 6 March, final readout 27 March.

Yusuf signed off first thing, so the Proseware observability pilot started on Wed 11 Feb, not the 9th. Agents going onto 14 of the 20 services today, the other 6 by Fri. Keeping the full 6 weeks means it now ends 25 Mar.

Fourth Coffee kiosk pilot went live today in all 12 Portland cafes. By 10am: 410 kiosk orders. Hawthorne St cafe had a card reader freeze around 8:15, rebooted and fine by 8:40. Offline mode test passed at both test cafes yesterday. Reggie happy so far.

Tailspin: Bettina says 31% of their contacts are 'where is my order'. She wants self-service order tracking in the Connect IVR, but not before the migration is done. Logged it as a post-migration idea, no promises.

prep for my 2:30 with Nkechi on the contract data cleanup. 11k records missing territory, she estimates 3 weeks by hand, cutover 6 Apr at risk and statements due 30 Apr. What options can I put to her to speed it up without burning her out?

Adatum: met Wendell Park, their SAP programme lead. They're moving to S/4HANA by 2028 and want a 6-week readiness assessment, proposal from us by 27 Feb. Anything unbudgeted over $100k needs board approval via Rosalind Featherstone, the CFO. Next board meeting is 12 March.

Northwind: sensors arrived this morning, install started on the first 10 trucks. Leah Morgan (Head of IT) needs our gateway security questionnaire back before anything connects to their TMS. Our IoT lead is on it, due Fri.

Prep me for the WWI EDI RFP response. Maeve's weighting: cost 40%, delivery approach 30%, references 20%, support 10%. We're planning $285k fixed for 62 trading partners. I hear Norvik Partners is bidding. What are our win themes and where are we weak?

Deepa wants the weekly QA metrics (defects found, escaped defects, automation coverage) as a CSV export every Monday by 10am instead of the PDF report. She pipes it into their own dashboard. Marek Dvorak (our delivery manager) is setting it up from next Monday.
what did we agree to credit Trey for the Jan Azure overrun again, and is it going on the Feb invoice?

Draft the cover email to Bogdan for the SIP (Corinne's doc goes attached). Felix signed the metadata POC at $14.5k, starts Mon 23 Feb. He also said, very casually, that he's had a demo from a Shopify agency for the bookstore. Our retainer ($26k/month) renews 1 May. Need to watch this.

Options email went to Leopold. Gareth called after: Leopold leans to B but wants $47/hr. Also an offshore shop is quoting them $41/hr, though Gareth doesn't think they'd switch mid-migration. Holding at $51 for now.

Northwind: Fatma says Samuel Osei (CFO) signs off the network renewal himself. Her tip: never show him a percentage without the dollar amount next to it, he hates doing the maths and sends things back.

Write the email to Saskia sending the SLA schedule and 2025 incident log she asked for. Be upfront about the Black Friday outage: 47 min, RCA done, $18k service credit paid in December. Short and factual, no spin.
